requirement: Add a new key, Reset (an administrator override). While "blocked", Reset returns the lock to "locked" with an empty buffer and a failure count of 0. While "locked" or "open", Reset is ignored (it changes nothing, not even the buffer).
desc: Simulate a keypad lock. code is a non-empty string of decimal digits. The lock starts "locked" with an empty entry buffer and a failure count of 0. While "locked": Digit(d) appends the digit d (0-9) to the buffer, but the buffer holds at most as many digits as code has, so when it is full the oldest digit is dropped first; Clear empties the buffer; Enter compares the buffer with code: if equal, the lock becomes "open" and the failure count resets to 0, otherwise the failure count goes up by 1 and, when it reaches 3, the lock becomes "blocked". Enter always empties the buffer. Clear does not reset the failure count. Reset is ignored. While "open": Enter makes it "locked" again (buffer empty, failure count still 0); Digit, Clear and Reset are ignored. While "blocked": Reset makes it "locked" again with an empty buffer and a failure count of 0; every other key is ignored. Return the final state: "locked", "open" or "blocked".

decls.canon:
type Key =
  | Digit(d: Int)
  | Enter
  | Clear
  | Reset
decls.ts: type Key = { kind: "Digit"; d: number } | { kind: "Enter" } | { kind: "Clear" } | { kind: "Reset" };
